title: The Fitbit Edge just made Google’s wearable lineup better than you think
summary: The latest fitness tracker is only part of a bigger plan.
body: None of us had it on our bingo cards this year, but Google has surprisingly emerged as the company with the best wearable ecosystem on the market. The new Fitbit Edge not only carries forward the legacy of the Fitbit Charge from the bygone era but also gives Google a solid chance to put its best foot forward in a wearable market that has already picked sides. But beyond a lineup that addresses (nearly) every consumer need on the spectrum, Google has, more importantly, created an underlying platform that is actually shaping its fitness ecosystem for the long run.

title: Samsung Health is making it easier to keep tabs on your runs and sleep
summary: Samsung Health’s sleep and running tools just got an upgrade.
body: TL;DR Samsung is rolling out a new Samsung Health update that focuses on sleep and running features. The update adds a new Sleep Balance graph that shows five sleep indicators at a glance. Running Coach now has two additional tiers, and the app supports Strava integration. Samsung gave its Health app a major update a few months ago, introducing several new tools to keep better track of your health. Now, the company is rolling out another update, this time focusing more on its sleep and running features. In a new blog post , the company announced a couple of noteworthy changes to the Samsung Health app. First, it’s lowering the data requirement to use Sleep Coaching. The feature originally required at least seven days of sleep tracking data in a month, but Samsung has lowered it to three days of sleep data within the past two weeks. Once users complete setup, Sleep Coaching gives them daily habit checklists and weekly recommendations to improve sleep.
